[Command Reference](changeHttpMonitorCompartment)
records: The [OCID] of the compartment into which the resource should be moved. [required]

For optimistic concurrency control. In the PUT or DELETE call for a resource, set the `if-match` parameter to the value of the etag from a previous GET or POST response for that resource.  The resource will be updated or deleted only if the etag you provide matches the resource's current etag value.

Provide input to this command as a JSON document from a file using the file://path-to/file syntax.

helpDoc.text:
Creates an HTTP monitor. Vantage points will be automatically selected if not specified, and probes will be initiated from each vantage point to each of the targets at the frequency specified by `intervalInSeconds`. 
[Command Reference](createHttpMonitor)
records:
A list of targets (hostnames or IP addresses) of the probe.
This is a complex type whose value must be valid JSON. The value can be provided as a string on the command line or passed in as a file using
the file://path/to/file syntax.

The --generate-param-json-input option can be used to generate an example of the JSON which must be provided. We recommend storing this example
in a file, modifying it as needed and then passing it back in via the file:// syntax.
 [required]
A user-friendly and mutable name suitable for display in a user interface. [required]
The monitor interval in seconds. Valid values: 10, 30, and 60. [required]

A list of names of vantage points from which to execute the probe.

The probe timeout in seconds. Valid values: 10, 20, 30, and 60. The probe timeout must be less than or equal to `intervalInSeconds` for monitors.
The optional URL path to probe, including query parameters.

A dictionary of HTTP request headers.

*Note:* Monitors and probes do not support the use of the `Authorization` HTTP header.
